Table 2: Business Model Market Products 33 6.1.12 Task 12.0: Evaluate Scalability and National Replication Potential This work builds on the Baseline Scalability and Replicability Report from Budget Period 1, which examined opportunities and barriers to scaling the UDERMS iCommunity approach. The report considered both the project’s current context and the broader conditions that will influence adoption and adaptation by other utilities across states and regions. The analysis focused on key domains relevant to scalability, including: • Grid services design for distributed energy resources (DERs) • Cybersecurity frameworks • Evaluation, measurement, and verification (EM&V) methods • Environmental policies and regulations • ISO/RTO and wholesale market participation • Public policy objectives affecting DER integration The report identified barriers to replication such as technology complexity, utility business models, regulatory requirements, and the cost and valuation of grid services. It also emphasized the role of economies of learning. Activities that are resource-intensive to establish the first time, such as cybersecurity planning, EM&V, participant recruitment, and DER control strategies, become easier, less costly, and more effective with repetition and knowledge sharing. These gains were to allow subsequent projects and utilities to scale more efficiently and avoid duplicating effort. While detailed quantitative lessons were not yet available, early findings suggest that replication will benefit from standardized approaches to DER communication protocols, data pathways, and enrollment procedures. Establishing these practices now creates a foundation for large-scale deployment and positions utilities to adopt demand-flexible DER integration more effectively. Contextual factors such as policy environments, regulatory frameworks, market design, and technology costs remain central in shaping utility motivation, and these will continue to be key considerations for future replication efforts. The evaluation conducted to date provides an initial framework for understanding the challenges and opportunities that affect scalability and replication, satisfying Milestone 12.01. While it does not capture every barrier or solution, it established a foundation that would have been expanded as additional project data and operational experience had become available in Budget Period 3. This early work was to position the team to refine its understanding, incorporate new insights, and strengthen the relevance of the framework as the project progresses. 6.1.13 Task 13: Implement Data Coordination The data coordination task was focused on the consideration of sensor needs, data governance and the implementation of the M&V assessment plan (Deliverable 6.0.2). These activities had postured the team with Milestone 13.0.1 - “implementing the data M&V plan with data collection initiated from partner sites” completed and on-track to produce Deliverable 13.0.1 - “Report on initial data collection as part of the M&V assessment plan” by the end of the budget period. Task 8 and Task 13 also maintained a synergistic relationship throughout the 34 budget period, enabling the alignment of DER control strategy, architecture, and communications with data coordination efforts. The consideration of sensor needs consisted of leveraging the updated network architecture diagram from Subtask 8.1.0 to understand how demand response signals would be communicated to each type of DER.
